2.4 teacher-labelled Cool-down: Constructing a Parallel Line (restricted task body)

Tasks.Prompt: Produce an original compass/straightedge pattern, record each move and the shading/colour convention, exchange only the written instructions with someone who has not seen it, compare their recreation, correct one ambiguous instruction, and submit the two drawings and revised instructions to your teacher.

Criteria.Criterion: Permitted straightedge/compass operations and correctly maintained given distances
Clear labels for centres, radii, intersections and ordered connections
Partner can independently reproduce a recognizably identical construction from text; drawings submitted
Identifies and revises a genuinely ambiguous step and documents colour/shading

Tasks.Accept: Any nondegenerate, reproducible original construction with clear teacher-verifiable invariants; not a single prescribed diagram
Tasks.Reject: Merely copying a provided picture or listing unspecified circles/lines; typed numeric answer alone

Tasks.Prompt: Construct a regular hexagon in a circle using one unchanged compass opening equal to its radius, label consecutive A,B,C,D,E,F and draw the extended lines AB and DE. Explain why the two infinite lines are parallel and specify every construction move.
Tasks.Exemplar: Six equal-radius steps yield six equilateral central triangles with angle 60 degrees. The diameter half-turn swaps side AB with DE, so AB and DE have the same direction and are distinct parallel lines.

Criteria.Criterion: Nonzero circle radius, six distinct consecutively labelled vertices
Fixed-radius compass step and lines AB and DE correctly drawn
Explicit proof by 180-degree central symmetry/angle relations, not by appearance
Precise reproducible instructions with centre/radius/labelled lines

Tasks.Accept: Clockwise or anticlockwise orientation; any rotation/translation of the construction
Tasks.Reject: A sketch with merely asserted parallelism without angle or symmetry reasoning

SourcePracticeAnalogues.EvidenceMode: Human teacher reviewed paper reasoning; original source figures NOT copied; source problem numbers 1–4 mapped by skill, not image

Items.Prompt: Start with distinct A and B. Write every compass and straightedge move to construct the line through the two intersections X,Y of circles centred A and B, each radius AB.
Items.Expected: Draw circles with centres A and B and radius AB; mark both intersections X,Y; draw the full line XY. Name nonzero starting segment.

Items.Prompt: Two circles each radius AB are centred at A and B. Their intersections are X,Y. A point E lies on the circle centred A. Which of AX, AY, BX, BY, AE must equal AB? Explain.
Items.Expected: All five lengths equal AB by membership on the appropriate radius-AB circles.

Items.Prompt: A circle centred at A passes through B and X, while a different circle centred at B passes through X and A. Explain why AX=BX=AB.
Items.Expected: AX and AB are radii of circle A; BX and BA are radii of circle B.

Items.Prompt: A compass opens to length PQ and makes a circle centred R. Point S lies on the circle; point T is not stated to lie on the circle. Which equality is guaranteed: RS=PQ or RT=PQ?
Items.Expected: Only RS=PQ is guaranteed by the circle radius; no statement about RT follows.
